subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental `claws add` be allowed to install or reuse a process-wide plugin using only its exact-plan consent, or must it require an explicit host-level grant or defer plugin mutation?
rationale: The branch intentionally treats plugins as shared host resources rather than agent-scoped capabilities; deciding whether the displayed plan is adequate authorization is a product and security-boundary choice, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Require host-level authorization
options.body: Add a distinct documented host-level grant for shared plugin mutation, or keep plugin package actions blocked until that grant contract exists.

options.title: Approve exact-plan consent
options.body: Accept the displayed exact plugin artifact, digest, runtime id, and owner-state plan as sufficient authorization for this experimental feature.

options.title: Defer shared plugins
options.body: Land only workspace-scoped skill installation and move shared-plugin lifecycle support to a later, separately approved design.

recommendation.title: Require host-level authorization
recommendation.body: Add a distinct documented host-level grant for shared plugin mutation, or keep plugin package actions blocked until that grant contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review history is the strongest available signal for the lifecycle invariants and package-owner boundary at issue.
